rittum: hand: rittēšu (UM.ME-šu, the signs UM, ME and ŠU) “his hand(s)”, with -šu “his”; Harper normalizes rit-tê-šu with an ending -ê whose grammar is not clear to me; the second sign (read ME) and the number, one hand or two, are both UNCERTAIN · noun
ḫabātum-D: UNCERTAIN verb, the D-stem (intensive) of ḫabātum “to rob, plunder”, taken here as “to destroy” from the sense of the law, not from the grammar: uḫtabbit (uḫ-tab-bi-it, perfect, 3rd singular) “he has destroyed (?)”, said of an eye · D-stem verb, sense uncertain
ḫapādum-D: UNCERTAIN verb, not met elsewhere in the code; D-stem present plural, read “to destroy” only because the law repays the offender with the same loss: uḫappadū (u-ḫa-ap-pa-du) “they shall destroy (?)”, said of the offender’s eye; the sense is UNCERTAIN · D-stem verb, sense uncertain
eṣemtum: bone (written with the Sumerogram NER.PAD.DU, the three signs NER, PAD and DU, with no ending written): eṣemti (construct, before a genitive) “the bone of”, eṣemtašu “his bone” (with -šu, accusative); the Akkadian ending is supplied from the grammar, the exact form UNCERTAIN, the word is not · noun, Sumerogram
šebērum: to break: ištebir (iš-te-bi-ir, perfect, 3rd singular) “he has broken”, išebbirū (i-še-ib-bi-ru, present, 3rd plural, with the b doubled) “they shall break” · verb
šinnum: tooth: šinni (ši-in-ni, construct) “the tooth of”, šinnašu (ši-in-na-šu, accusative + -šu) “his tooth” · noun
mēḫrum: equal, counterpart (one of the same rank): mēḫrišu (me-iḫ-ri-šu, with -šu) “his equal”, said of a man who stands level with the offender; the sense comes from the form and the law, matching ša kīma šuāti “who is like him” · noun
lētum: cheek (the dictionary sense “cheek, jaw”): lēt (li-e-it, construct, before a genitive) “the cheek of”; UNCERTAIN, not derivable from the grammar · noun, sense uncertain
elī: over, above, upon (preposition): with the suffix, elišu (e-li-šu) “over him”, ša elišu rabû “who is great over him”, i.e. “who is greater than he” · preposition
qinazum: whip, thong (the dictionary sense), UNCERTAIN: qinazi (genitive, after ina “with”) “with a whip”, written with the hide determinative {mašak} and the group qi₂-na-az; Harper lists the three pieces as one sign, so the split into syllables is a reconstruction and UNCERTAIN · noun, sense uncertain
šūši: sixty (written with the Sumerogram ŠU.ŠI, the signs ŠU and ŠI, preceded by the wedge 1): 1 šūši “sixty”; the thing counted (strokes) is not written · numeral
maḫāṣum-N: N-stem (passive) of maḫāṣum “to strike”: to be struck: immaḫḫaṣ (im-maḫ-ḫa-aṣ, present, 3rd singular) “he shall be struck” · N-stem verb
uznum: ear: uznašu (written u-zu-un-šu, with no vowel between un and šu; Harper normalizes accusative + -šu) “his ear”; the noun has no plural ending here, so one ear · noun
risbatum: brawl, quarrel (Harper’s sense), UNCERTAIN, the word is not met elsewhere: risbatim (ri-is-ba-tim, genitive after ina) “in a brawl” · noun, sense uncertain
ṣimmum: wound (Harper’s sense), UNCERTAIN, not derivable from the grammar: ṣimmam (ṣi-im-ma-am, accusative) “a wound”; the first sign is the sign ZI in the autograph (Harper prints zi-im-ma-am here), read ṣi · noun, sense uncertain
tamûm: to swear (an oath): itamma (i-tam-ma, present, 3rd singular) “he shall swear”, itammama (i-tam-ma-ma) “he shall swear, and”, with -ma · verb
asûm: physician (written with the Sumerogram A.ZU, the signs A and ZU, with no ending written): asâm (accusative, read from the context) “the physician”: asâm ippal “he shall pay the physician” · noun, Sumerogram

__broaden__.nadûm-Š: Š-stem of nadûm “to throw”: to make (someone) throw down, to strip of: uštaddišu (perfect, with -šu) “he made him throw (it) down” · make her drop, of a woman and what is in her womb: uštaddīši (uš-ta-di-ši, uš-ta-ad-di-ši, perfect, with -ši “her”) “he has made her drop”, i.e. made her miscarry; the geminate d is spelled once or twice
__broaden__.šīmum: purchase, purchase price · šīmišu (ŠÁM-šu, with -šu “his”) “his price”, of a slave: mišil šīmišu “half of his price”
__broaden__.nadûm: to cast, throw (a charge; a body into the river): iddi, nadû, iddû · also to leave lying (a field): ittadi “he has left (it) lying” · of a flock: ṣēnī ana eqlim iddi “he turned the sheep loose into a field” · inaddûši (i-na-[ad]-du-u-ši) “they shall throw her” (present, plural, with -ši): ana mê inaddûši “they shall throw her into the water” · inaddûši “they shall throw him” of a man (§155, ana mê inaddûši), UNCERTAIN because the suffix -ši is “her” elsewhere · of a tooth, to knock out: ittadi (it-ta-di, perfect) “he has knocked out”, inaddû (i-na-ad-du-u, present plural) “they shall knock out”: šinni awīlim ittadi “he has knocked out a man’s tooth”
__broaden__.maḫāṣum: to strike; of ground, to break up: imaḫḫaṣ “he shall break up” · the noun maḫāṣum “beating, abuse, injury” (Harper), written ma-ḫa-ṣi-im with the sign ZI (value ṣi): maḫāṣim “(through) beating” · imtaḫaṣ (im-ta-ḫa-aṣ, perfect) “he has struck”, imḫaṣma (preterite + -ma), amḫaṣ “I struck”: amḫassu (am-ḫa-zu) “I struck him” (ṣ + š said ss, written with ZU); the infinitive maḫāṣišu (ma-ḫa-zi-šu) “his striking, his blow”, ina maḫāṣišu “from his blow”
__broaden__.nakāsum: to cut, cut down: ikkis (preterite) “he cut down” · inakkisū (i-na-ak-ki-su) “they shall cut off”, present plural (the ending -sū is written with the one sign su, as Harper prints it): lišānšu inakkisū “they shall cut off his tongue”, tulêša inakkisū “they shall cut off her breast” · inakkisū “they shall cut off”, of the hand(s) and the ear: rittēšu inakkisū “they shall cut off his hand(s)”, uznašu inakkisū “they shall cut off his ear”
__broaden__.edûm: to know; mūdi “knower of”; īdû “he knows” · idû (i-du-u) taken as the infinitive “knowing” after ina: ina idû lā amḫassu “in knowing, I did not strike him”, i.e. “I did not strike him knowingly”, UNCERTAIN as a parse
__broaden__.libbum: heart · ana libbi “into”: ana libbi zittišu “into his share” · libbaša, libbiša (li-ib-ba-ša, li-ib-bi-ša) “her heart”: mala libbiša “as much as her heart wants”; libbaša uṭabbū “they shall make her heart good”, i.e. content her · ša libbiša (li-ib-bi-ša) “what is in her womb”, literally “that of her heart”, the unborn child: ana ša libbiša “for what was in her womb”
__broaden__.mārtum: daughter (written DUMU+ti): mārtišu “his daughter” · mārassu (DUMU.SAL-zu, three signs DUMU + SAL + ZU, ZU for -ssu) “his daughter” · mārtaka (DUMU.SAL-ka) “your daughter”, mārtī (DUMU.SAL-i) “my daughter”, mārtim (DUMU.SAL, no ending written) “of the daughter”: abī mārtim “the father of the daughter” · mārtišu also written DUMU.SAL-šu (DUMU + SAL + ŠU) “his daughter”: ana mārtišu “to his daughter” · mārat (DUMU.SAL, no ending written) construct “daughter of”: mārat awīlim “a man’s daughter”, mārat muškēnim “a commoner’s daughter”
__broaden__.amtum: slave-woman (GEME₂) · amassu (GEME₂-zu) “his slave-woman”, amtam (GEME₂-am), amtim (GEME₂-tim) · plural amâti (GEME₂{meš}) “slave-women”; the exact plural signs are UNCERTAIN · amat (GEME₂, the two signs SAL and KUR, no ending written) construct “slave-woman of”: amat awīlim “a man’s slave-woman”
